scope: New Go domain types only, in internal/pipeline: a Stage type, the canonical 7-stage order, and a pure forward-transition check, plus a table-driven test. No orchestrator, no run.go/service.go, no stage handlers, no stages/ subpackage, no I/O, no HTTP wiring, no LLM calls. Matches build-order step 3 ('pipeline/ domain core: run.go, stage.go, transition.go + tests — the state machine, no I/O') minus run.go, which is a separate future task not covered by this task's stated focus.

acceptance_criteria.text: Stage constants exactly match the 7 pipeline_stage enum values and order from thinkboard-schema-final.sql: scope_anchor, analytic, research, validation, questioning, research_scoped, result.
Exactly one exported declaration in the package enumerates stage order; no other file/function in the diff repeats the sequence as a literal list.
Allowed(from, to) is true only when to is the immediate successor of from in the canonical order; false for backward, skip, self, and any invalid Stage value.
transition_test.go is table-driven, covers all 6 valid forward pairs, and covers rejected backward/skip/self/unknown cases; go test passes.

open_questions: 03-backend-folder-architecture.md §5.1's file tree puts stage.go and transition.go directly under internal/pipeline/, but puts registry.go ("the ONLY declaration of stage order") under the internal/pipeline/stages/ subpackage. Taken literally that's a package cycle: stages/registry.go needs pipeline.Stage (child importing parent), and transition.go would need to read order from stages/registry.go (parent importing child). Resolution used here: since build-order step 3 (§10) scopes this task to run.go/stage.go/transition.go only — no stages/ subpackage, no handlers — the canonical order is declared once in internal/pipeline/stage.go itself (the only place in this diff that lists the 7 stages), and transition.go derives Allowed() from that slice instead of repeating it. The literal stages/registry.go (map[Stage]Handler) is deferred to the task that adds the first real stage handler (build-order step 4+), which should import internal/pipeline for Stage/Order rather than redeclaring them. Flagging this instead of silently building the stages/ subpackage now, since the user's stated task focus (Stage, canonical order, forward transitions, registry-as-only-order-source) is fully satisfied without it and adding an empty subpackage would be speculative scaffolding.
risks: If a later task creates internal/pipeline/stages/registry.go without importing this task's Order/Stage, the codebase would end up with two declarations of stage order, breaking the single-source rule this task establishes.
